comparison: Perfect agreement on zebrafish model establishment (C3, C23-C28, C67-C69). Both evaluations find the hyperangiogenic phenotype well-characterized and supported by experimental evidence across multiple treatment windows and imaging data. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Complete agreement on arterial/venous characterization (C34). Both evaluations accept this observational finding from transgenic reporter imaging without concerns. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on uncertainty regarding translational implications (C81-C82). Both evaluations acknowledge the zebrafish findings but express caution about extrapolating to human ASB consumption and health implications. Both rate as UNCERTAIN, citing need for mammalian/human validation.

Strong agreement on noncaloric monosaccharide effects (C4, C29-C33, C79, C83, C85). Both evaluations confirm glucose and noncaloric monosaccharides induce excessive vessel formation, with appropriate osmotic and caloric controls. OpenEval includes additional claims C84, C86 about disaccharide conversion. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on tip cell activation mechanism (C5, C35-C39). Both evaluations confirm quiescent endothelial cells convert to proliferating tip cells based on imaging evidence. OpenEval additionally references molecular validation (C47) and lack of perfusion (C87). Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on single-cell RNA-seq analysis (C40-C51). Both evaluations accept the clustering, cell type identification, and differential expression findings. Peer review explicitly includes C6 and C47 in their evaluation while OpenEval groups C47 with R3. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Substantial agreement on foxo1a downregulation and functional role (C52-C56, C72-C74). Both evaluations confirm foxo1a involvement through loss-of-function and rescue experiments. OpenEval emphasizes the partial rescue and literature context (C72-C73), while peer review integrates pathway conclusions (C7, C66, C74). Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on marcksl1a regulation and foxo1a-marcksl1a pathway (C57-C65). Both evaluations confirm the regulatory relationship through gain/loss-of-function, ChIP-PCR, and luciferase assays. OpenEval includes additional supporting details (C88-C89 on sequence conservation). Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on integrated pathway conclusions (C7, C65-C66, C74). OpenEval focuses on marcksl1a knockdown rescue experiments and pathway generality, while peer review groups these pathway conclusions with foxo1a findings. Both rate as SUPPORTED but organize the evidence differently.

OpenEval evaluates epidemiological background claims (C1, C2, C13-C17, C75-C78) establishing study context and motivation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically focus on novel findings rather than literature review sections. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates background literature on diabetes complications and vascular pathology (C8-C12, C70-C71, C80). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are established facts from cited literature. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates zebrafish model rationale and knowledge gap claims (C18-C22). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focus on experimental findings rather than methodological justification sections. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED.
